questions.question: A triangle in which all three sides have distinct, unequal lengths is called a ____ triangle.

solution_key.part3_conclusion: By classification: Equilateral has 3 equal sides, Isosceles has 2 equal sides, and Scalene has 3 unequal sides.

questions.question: Two sides of a triangle measure 6 cm and 10 cm. What is the allowable range of lengths for the third side 'x'?
questions.hint_modal: Recall core principles from Chapter 7: Upper limit: x < 6 + 10 => x < 16 cm. Lower limit: x + 6 > 1...

solution_key.part2_method: Apply exact mathematical formula or logical deduction step
solution_key.part3_conclusion: Upper limit: x < 6 + 10 => x < 16 cm. Lower limit: x + 6 > 10 => x > 4 cm. Thus, 4 cm < x < 16 cm.

questions.question: A surveyor maps three town positions A, B, C with road distances AB = 12 km, BC = 20 km, and AC = 40 km. The map claims A, B, C form a triangular path. Is this claim accurate? Explain.
questions.hint_modal: Recall core principles from Chapter 7: Sum of two shorter distances AB + BC = 12 + 20 = 32 km. Long...

solution_key.part2_method: Apply exact mathematical formula or logical deduction step
solution_key.part3_conclusion: Sum of two shorter distances AB + BC = 12 + 20 = 32 km. Longest distance AC = 40 km. Since 32 km < 40 km, the sum of two sides is less than the third side, violating the Triangle Inequality Theorem. Towns A, B, C cannot form a triangle.

hotspots.title: Direct Path vs Detour
hotspots.popover_content: Direct straight path c is strictly shorter than detour path a + b (c < a + b => a + b > c).

hotspots.title: Triangle Inequality Theorem
hotspots.popover_content: Sum of any 2 sides > 3rd side (a+b>c, b+c>a, c+a>b). Test: Smallest two sum > longest side.

hotspots.title: Side-Based Classification
hotspots.popover_content: Equilateral (a=b=c, always valid for s>0), Isosceles (a=b!=c), Scalene (a!=b!=c).

hotspots.title: Compass Arc Construction
hotspots.popover_content: Compass arcs of radii a and b intersect to locate 3rd vertex iff a + b > c. Arcs fail if a + b <= c.
